title: Fill-Only worker result
description: What comes back from a worker: hashes and stable codes, never observed values or page text. The worker is an untrusted executor and fill_core is the authority, so every field here is checked on the way in and every check fails closed.

final_action_activations.description: The target's own count, or null when the target keeps none and the run could not observe it. Null is not a zero: `validate_result` refuses it, so `fill_core` cannot import an unprovable run as a safe one. On the local replay this is a real oracle — a test clicks the control without the guard and it reaches one. On a supervised live page there is no counter, and the equivalent is a scoped guard installed for the run (capture-phase submit block plus unexpected-navigation detection) removed before control returns to the user. Upload traffic is separately allowed and validated, because a file upload is a POST and 'block all POST' is not submission protection. The two must not be reported as the same evidence.

error_code.description: A closed vocabulary. A length bound is not value-free: 64 characters is room for a short answer or a line of page text.

results.description: One entry per issued action, in the order they were issued. Missing, extra, duplicated and reordered results all fail closed. `not_attempted` means execution stopped at an earlier violation and this action was never run — deliberately distinct from `refused`, so which action caused the stop stays legible.

$comment: Refused anywhere at any depth: value, values, text, inner_text, html, outer_html, content, label, options, cookie, cookies, token, session_token, authorization, path, file_path, local_path, screenshot, page_text, answer. Options in particular are transient observation data only and never reach a persisted observation.
